subject: Private deployment: access & firewall sweep for upcoming activation
messages:
From: Alice Nguyen <alice@novamed.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-04T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private deployment: initial network preflight

Hi Jasmine,

We're aiming to flip the private deployment switch for NovaMed next week (targeting 2027-05-11). Before the activation I'd like to confirm network/readiness items so we don't hit delays during the maintenance window. Can you send over a concise list of the exact access rules, service IPs, and any service account/service-account-email whitelists you need?

We have our infra team (infra-ops@novamed.com) on the thread. Key constraints: we run behind an on-prem perimeter firewall, strict egress controls, and an internal NAT pool. Also we need to capture what evidence Redwood will need for final signoff (traces, test responses, sample logs).

Thanks,
Alice Nguyen
Head of Infrastructure, NovaMed Health

Date: 2027-05-04T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: initial network preflight

Hi Alice — thanks for the context and timeline.

Summary: below is a compact preflight checklist and the minimal firewall/ACL requirements for our Private (VPC/on-prem) activation. I attached a one‑page PDF checklist and a CSV template for your firewall team to populate (attached as 20270504-novamed-firewall-request.csv).

Action items (high priority before 2027-05-11):
- Network: allow outbound TLS (443) from our runtime nodes to the following IPs (see CSV). These are for control plane telemetry and image pull.
- Ports: open inbound TCP 8910 from your management jump hosts to the onboarding bastion only (temporary, removed after handoff).
- DNS: ensure private namespace resolves our service hostname (provided in the CSV) to the assigned private IPs.
- Service accounts: add redwood-service@novamed-iam.svc as a trusted service account for vault access during provisioning (details under "Service account notes").
- Evidence: run curl test to the readiness endpoint (we'll provide the exact path) and capture HTTP 200 with expected JSON schema. Provide NAT translation logs for the provisioning window.

Ben and Karthik are looped for the detailed port/IP matrix below. If your team prefers, we can do a 30-minute walkthrough today or tomorrow to walk the firewall admin through the CSV fields.

Regards,
Jasmine Liu
Account Manager, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1-415-555-0119

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-04T11:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: initial network preflight (port/IP matrix)

Hi team — technical details below for NovaMed's network team. I've kept this minimal — these are the values we must see green before we run provisioning.

Port/IP matrix (minimal set):
- Outbound: TCP 443 to control.redwood-api-us-1.redwood.net (resolve to ELB IPs in CSV) — used for model catalog and control handshake.
- Outbound: TCP 5222 to telemetry-redwood-us.redwood.net (TLS over 5222) — used for metrics streaming; allow to the IP range listed.
- Inbound: TCP 8910 (onboarding SSH/tunnel) — restrict to management jump host(s) only. We'll provide the temporary public keys.
- DNS: split-horizon DNS entry under myproject.redwood.local -> private IPs we assign during provisioning.
- Egress NAT: ensure SNAT mapping preserves source port range 49152-65535 for token exchange.

Additional notes:
- We recommend keeping port 8910 closed after activation; the runtime will be reachable via your internal load balancer and the assigned private IPs.
- For air-gapped customers: provide OCI/registry mirror credentials; not required for NovaMed based on current plan.

Test checklist (what we'll run after you apply rules):
1) Connectivity test: curl -kv "https://CONTROL_ENDPOINT/healthz" -> expect 200 and JSON {"status":"ok"}.
2) KV access: small Put/Get to KMS-backed Vault (provide logs).
3) Latency smoke: tokenized generate call to sample model with 512 context to verify <120ms p50 for internal traffic (informational).

If infra can populate the CSV and send back by EOD we'll queue provisioning for 2027-05-06. Happy to jump on a call — propose 2027-05-04 15:00 PST if that works.

- Ben
Principal Onboarding Engineer, Redwood Inference

Also sending the filled CSV as 20270504-novamed-firewall-request.csv and a short firewall rule export. We will also provide the NAT translation logs during the provisioning window.
